marks.gloss_en: the suspicion reason speaks of a NEW ruin, where there is no danger of collapse
the suspicion reason speaks of TWO DISSOLUTE men -- two are not threatened by demons, and though two are ordinarily above suspicion, dissolute men are not
the collapse reason speaks of TWO UPSTANDING men -- no suspicion, no demons, yet the ruin may collapse
the demons reason speaks of two [upstanding men, in a new ruin] in the demons' own haunt -- there we fear demons even for two
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: before the dead one says nothing but the dead man's own matters
version 1: the dictum was said only of words of Torah; worldly talk before the dead is not restricted
version 2: the dictum was said even of words of Torah -- and all the more so worldly talk is barred before the dead
מאי קרא? ואחרי אחיתפל בניהו בן יהוידע ואביתר ושר צבא למלך יואב -- the verse's order is the aggada's order: adviser, Sanhedrin, Urim veTumim, general
the verse: 'and after Achitofel, Benayahu son of Yehoyada and Evyatar, and the general of the king's army, Yoav' (I Chr 27:34)
וכן הוא אומר: ועצת אחיתפל אשר יעץ... כאשר ישאל איש בדבר האלהים
Achitofel in the verse stands for the adviser
ודוד בפלגא דליליא הוה קאי? מאורתא הוה קאי! דכתיב קדמתי בנשף ואשועה -- and neshef is evening (Prov 7:9)
the verse: 'I rose with the neshef and cried out' (Ps 119:147) -- David rose at neshef
אמר רב אושעיא אמר רבי אחא: הכי קאמר דוד -- midnight never passed me in sleep; he rose by neshef when he could, but never slept past midnight
R' Acha: David meant -- midnight never passed me by in sleep (sometimes he rose at neshef, but never later than midnight)
until midnight he dozed like a horse, from then on he roused himself like a lion -- both verses describe one night
until midnight Torah (קדמתי בנשף... לדברך), from midnight songs and praises (חצות לילה אקום להודות לך)
R' Zeira: until midnight David dozed like a horse; from then on he roused himself like a lion
ונשף אורתא הוא? הא נשף צפרא הוא! דכתיב ויכם דוד מהנשף ועד הערב למחרתם -- מאי לאו מצפרא ועד ליליא?
the verse: 'and David smote them from the neshef until the evening of the next day' (I Sam 30:17)
אלא אמר רבא: תרי נשפי הוו -- the word names both transitions, so Prov 7:9's neshef is evening and I Sam 30:17's is morning
Rava: there are two neshefs -- the night departs and day comes (morning), the day departs and night comes (evening)
ודוד מי הוה ידע פלגא דליליא אימת? השתא משה רבינו לא הוה ידע -- כחצות הלילה; God said בחצות and Moshe said כחצות, so Moshe was uncertain -- ודוד הוה ידע?!
the verse: 'about midnight I will go out into the midst of Egypt' (Ex 11:4) -- Moshe's 'about'
דוד סימנא הוה ליה -- the lyre over his bed played of itself at midnight (R' Shimon Chasida via Rav Acha bar Bizna)
David had a sign for midnight: a lyre hung over his bed; when midnight came the north wind blew through it and it played of itself, and he rose at once and studied Torah until dawn
one verse: David rose at midnight (Ps 119:62)
(entertained) the verse means from one evening to the next evening -- so neshef is evening after all
(entertained) it was the Holy One Himself who said 'about midnight' to Moshe
at once they take counsel with Achitofel, consult the Sanhedrin, and ask the Urim veTumim (and only then, 4a.2, the general Yoav)
ורבי נתן סבר לה כרבי יהושע -- with kings rising at three hours, David's midnight rise preceded them by two full four-hour watches, so 'kidmu einai ashmurot' holds under three watches
R' Yehoshua's mishnah (Berakhot 9b): the morning Shema may be recited until three hours, for kings rise at three hours
the night consists of four watches
'the middle watch' (Jud 7:19) entails exactly one watch before it and one after -- three in all
Rebbi's reading: 'tikhona' is one of the two middle watches of four
Rav Ashi: a watch and a half [elapsed by midnight under three watches] is also called 'watches'
